title: Urgent priming-lag: correct worker affinity and queue prioritization
creator: Avery Patel
description: After the kernel-affinity heuristic rollout (runtime-1.21-canary) we observed an intermittent priming-lag affecting small-context (<64 tokens) requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Symptoms: elevated time-to-first-token (TTFT) spikes, stepwise drop in tokens/sec for multiplexed workers, and oscillations in per-worker tail latency during load. Root cause appears to be a race between the new kernel-selector rebind and queue reprioritization that moved short-context traffic to cold workers and then back, causing repeated KV cache misses and CPU/GPU kernel thrashing.
observed_metrics: TTFT p95 increased from 110ms -> 420ms for short-context chat model variants
ongoing spike correlation with canary kernel-selector enablement timestamps
increase in KV cache miss rate and higher GPU kernel launch variance
actions_taken: Rolled feature-flag back in Hosted canary and paused Dedicated auto-rollout (2026-03-10 21:10 UTC)
Applied emergency router config to pin short-context traffic to warm pools for affected customers
Deployed kernel-affinity patch to preserve stable affinity mapping when queue reprioritization triggers
Added 50ms hysteresis delay before kernel selector changes to avoid oscillation
Enabled verbose telemetry for affinity mapping and queue transitions
rollback_plan: If residual regressions persist, fully revert runtime-1.21 canary and route all traffic to runtime-1.20 warm pool (fast rollback path exists)
Notify Dedicated customers and flip manual routing to pre-rollout GPUs for their workloads
